title: Rust: FFI and Unsafe Code
description: Work with unsafe Rust and simulate Foreign Function Interface (FFI) patterns.

steps.title: Unsafe Block
steps.description: Create a raw pointer from a reference and dereference it inside an `unsafe` block. Print the value through the raw pointer.

verification.failureMessage: Create a raw pointer and print its value.

steps.title: Mutable Raw Pointer
steps.description: Create a mutable raw pointer and modify the value through it. Print the value before and after the unsafe modification.
hints: `let mut x = 10; let raw = &mut x as *mut i32;`

verification.failureMessage: Modify a value through a mutable raw pointer.

steps.title: Calling a C Function (Simulated)
steps.description: Use `extern "C"` block to declare a function (simulated by actually implementing it). Call the function and print the result. Use `unsafe` to call it.
hints: `extern "C" fn add_c(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32 { a + b }`
Call via function pointer: `let f: extern "C" fn(i32, i32) -> i32 = add_c;`

verification.failureMessage: Define and call a C-ABI function that adds two numbers.

steps.title: Union and Transmute
steps.description: Use `std::mem::transmute` to convert between types: transmute a `u32` to `f32` and print the result. Also demonstrate unsafe union access.

verification.failureMessage: Transmute u32 bits to f32 and print Pi.

steps.title: Safe FFI Wrapper
steps.description: Create a safe wrapper around an unsafe C-like API. Define an opaque handle type, a create/destroy pair, and safe Rust functions that wrap unsafe calls.
hints: `impl Handle { fn new() -> Self { unsafe { Handle(create()) } } }`
`impl Drop for Handle { fn drop(&mut self) { unsafe { destroy(self.0) } } }`

verification.failureMessage: Create a safe wrapper around an unsafe API and use it.
